inherited_mathematical_inputs: D99: the actual stable reduction graph, positive thicknesses, and nonhyperellipticity.
D102: principal-parts/residue-index theorem and its still-unverified actual divisor/model hypotheses.
D104: integral ramification derivative, Hodge/stable comparison, and saved CM Hodge-height interval.
D105--D106: Hilbert class field, CM orbit, rational descent and residue frame.
D110--D112: actual dyadic uniformization, exact CM coordinate matrices, trivial norm-one stabilizers at all seventeen CM points.
D115--D116: frozen P=200 actual leading coefficients, stable integral harmonic basis, fibre exponents 296/33, and actual section valuation bounds.
D116--D117: integral quadric tensor and successive nodal jets, uniform disk of radius squared 3/5 and exact-zero criterion.
new_deductions: Compute the two finite CM height corrections together via the composite derivative W_C -> L(Q)^2 on a small-level model.
The integral Hodge generator dz/z=2dw/(1-w^2) gives exact contents m_i-16, hence 280 at W and 17 at each other CM point.
Galois averaging yields exact combined dyadic correction (69/34)*log(2), and H_CM <=2*h_L-(35/34)*log(2)<8/3.
The known length-76 graph has tau=67889/27075 and tropical moment 223268/27075.
Final sufficient section-valuation thresholds are 25330/25444/25551; the fixed-input radius-one limits are 22310/22412/22506.
Known common vertical content already included in the measured zero degree cannot be counted again as a height improvement.

independent_methods: Revalue all 272 leading coefficient vectors in the degree-16 Eisenstein basis.
Direct coordinate differentiation for the composite local derivative.
Verify the graph Laplacian inverse by exact matrix multiplication.
Integrate squared resistance derivatives by exact Simpson quadrature at every basepoint.
Use a separate rational logarithm series to check both intermediate and final budgets.

next_bounded_research_task: Test a lower-degree integral CM residue-frame construction through D102's principal-parts sequence, first constructing and checking an actual finite flat Cartier CM divisor and its intersection/principal-part/cohomology data. No smaller bound from this route is yet proved.
